question: I manually stopped a container that has the restart policy `always`. What happens to it when the Docker daemon restarts?

### `restart`

`restart` defines the policy that the platform applies on container termination.

- `no`: The default restart policy. It does not restart the container under any circumstances.
- `always`: The policy always restarts the container until its removal.
- `on-failure[:max-retries]`: The policy restarts the container if the exit code indicates an error.
Optionally, limit the number of restart retries the Docker daemon attempts.
- `unless-stopped`: The policy restarts the container irrespective of the exit code but stops
  restarting when the service is stopped or removed.

```yml
    restart: "no"
    restart: always
    restart: on-failure
    restart: on-failure:3
    restart: unless-stopped
```

You can find more detailed information on restart policies in the
[Restart Policies (--restart)](/reference/cli/docker/container/run/#restart)
section of the Docker run reference page.

### `runtime`

answer: When the Docker daemon restarts, a container with the `always` restart policy will be automatically restarted. Since you manually stopped the container but the `always` policy is still in effect, the container will resume operation upon the next Docker daemon start.
